title: Site readiness check — customer network & install observations (Oct 2026)
summary: Working notes from the lightweight site-readiness program we ran for three customers during the first two weeks of Oct 2026. Purpose: identify recurring friction points for on-prem/VPC installs and produce prescriptive preflight checks for Solutions/Field. This doc combines standup snippets, recurring blockers, and immediate mitigations to fold into the preflight checklist and the new field runbook template.
standup_notes:
Day-by-day highlights across three sites (Acme Logistics, Meridian Health, Nimbus Analytics). Quick bullets: 
- Oct 02: initial network topology audit revealed inconsistent NAT implementation at Acme (customer IT had port mappings that conflicted with our egress nodes). 
- Oct 03: Meridian has a corporate proxy that does deep TLS inspection; caused cert pinning failures in our control-plane agent. Workaround: proxy bypass for KMS traffic configured. 
- Oct 04: Nimbus reported NVidia driver mismatch on GPU hosts (driver 520 vs required 535) — blocked model validation tests. Field installed matching driver, but time-to-resolution was ~6 hours. 
- Oct 05: Across all sites we observed NTP skew > 3s on at least one node which triggered internal lease flaps; added NTP checks to preflight and recommended cron enforcement. 
- Oct 06: BGP peering expectation mismatch at Acme — they expected to push full route tables; our design expects selective route advertisement. Added a customer-ready diagram to reduce ambiguity. 
- Oct 07: Final sync — validated telemetry pipelines and confirmed roll-forward plan for Meridian (cert rotation and proxy exception).
customer_sites: Acme Logistics — midwest data center (private rack + VPC egress)
Meridian Health — hospital colo cluster (air-gapped sections + corporate proxy)
recent_actions: Deployed temporary control-plane bypass on Meridian to confirm KMS handshake without TLS MITM
Published driver compatibility matrix for GPU hosts and pushed to Solutions playbook
Added MTU and NTP checks to preflight script v0.4
Created visual network expectation diagram for Acme and sent to customer IT
blockers: Corporate TLS interception (Meridian) causing client cert validation failures
GPU driver (Nimbus) incompatible with compiled kernels causing slow fallback and test flakiness
BGP routing policy mismatch (Acme) — customer advertises full table which conflicts with our expected selective advertisement
Intermittent DNS resolution failures inside customer net that surface only under load
Library ABI mismatch on older RHEL nodes causing agent segfaults
mitigations: For TLS interception: recommend explicit KMS & control-plane bypass CIDRs in customer proxy, documented exceptions + test script to validate handshake
For GPU drivers: include automated driver/version scanner in preflight with one-command installer links for supported drivers
For BGP: produce two network diagrams (our expected advertising vs customer current state) and include a short checklist for peering policy negotiation
For DNS: ship a light-weight DNS stress test (udp/tcp, parallel queries) with guidance to check EDNS/forwarders
For ABI issues: add an agent compatibility check that validates glibc/kernel headers and suggests distro upgrade or containerized agent option
decisions: Ship preflight v0.4 with MTU, NTP, GPU-driver, DNS, and proxy/TLS checks as the minimum required for any scheduled install
Field will not attempt kernel-level fixes during regular installs — escalate to escalation-engineering for sustained ABI/kernel issues
Create a short internal training (20–30m) for Solutions on interpreting BGP diagrams and negotiating peering expectations with customers
